title: AI for Cybersecurity
summary: Use AI responsibly for code review, finding triage, learning, and workflow automation.

lessons.title: Safe AI-assisted security workflows
lessons.summary: Keep humans accountable and avoid exposing secrets.
lessons.content: Minimize sensitive data sent to providers, validate AI-generated claims, test prompts against untrusted input, and require human review before changes or external actions. Keep API keys server-side and enforce budgets and quotas.

quiz.question: Where should a production AI API key be stored?
options: In a protected server-side secret store
quiz.explanation: A server-side secret store or protected environment secret prevents exposing credentials to browser users.

lessons.title: Prompt injection defenses and LLM guardrails
lessons.summary: Mitigate indirect prompt injection, data poisoning, and unauthorized tool calls.
lessons.content: Prompt injections occur when untrusted input hijacks the system instructions of an LLM. Defenses include input sanitization, semantic classification guardrails, principle of least privilege on tool calls, and strict human-in-the-loop approvals for destructive operations.

quiz.question: What is an indirect prompt injection attack?
options: Embedding malicious adversarial instructions inside untrusted third-party data retrieved by the model
quiz.explanation: Indirect prompt injection occurs when external content (web pages, emails, database records) contains hidden prompt instructions parsed as commands by the model.
